subsystems.name: Electrode leads
subsystems.role: deliver stimulation and record neural activity at precise brain targets.

subsystems.name: Implantable pulse generator
subsystems.role: houses the battery, stimulation circuits and sensing electronics in the chest.

subsystems.name: Biomarker detection
subsystems.role: extracts real-time features from brain signals that mark a depressed or OCD state.

subsystems.name: Control algorithm
subsystems.role: decides when and how much to stimulate based on the sensed biomarker.

subsystems.name: External programmer
subsystems.role: lets clinicians tune sensing and stimulation parameters and review data.

subsystems.name: Power and data link
subsystems.role: supplies energy and moves data between implanted and external parts.

buildSteps.title: Find a biomarker
buildSteps.detail: Analyse intracranial recordings from patients with implanted electrodes to identify patterns — such as specific frequency bands or bursts — that correlate with depression or OCD symptoms.

buildSteps.title: Choose and validate targets
buildSteps.detail: Select brain regions such as the subcallosal cingulate or ventral capsule/ventral striatum, confirmed by imaging and temporary stimulation.

buildSteps.title: Design the electrode
buildSteps.detail: Fabricate a flexible lead with multiple small contacts (millimetre scale) that can both stimulate and record without damaging tissue.

buildSteps.title: Build the pulse generator
buildSteps.detail: Engineer a chest-implanted device with a sensing front-end, a programmable stimulator, and enough battery capacity for years of intermittent therapy.

buildSteps.title: Write the control loop
buildSteps.detail: Implement an algorithm on the device that detects the biomarker in real time and triggers stimulation only when needed, with hard limits to prevent harm.

buildSteps.title: Test in animals
buildSteps.detail: Verify safety, longevity and efficacy in rodents and non-human primates, including long-term implantation.

buildSteps.title: Run clinical trials
buildSteps.detail: Start with small safety trials, then larger trials that compare closed-loop stimulation with sham or fixed stimulation for depression and OCD.

buildSteps.title: Secure approval and scale
buildSteps.detail: Obtain regulatory approval for specific indications, then train surgical teams and build programming support.

prerequisites.why: Decades of use in movement disorders prove that implanted electrodes can safely modulate brain circuits.
Candidate signals have been found in small studies, but no biomarker reliably tracks depression or OCD across patients.
Closed-loop sensing is already used in epilepsy, but psychiatric signals are slower and more variable.
Simple threshold-based control exists, but psychiatric states need models that adapt to each patient.
Rechargeable batteries and inductive charging are mature from cardiac and neurostimulation devices.

pathway.milestone: closed-loop neurostimulation is approved for epilepsy; early trials test sensing-enabled DBS in depression and OCD
pathway.unlocks: proof that biomarkers can be recorded and used to trigger stimulation in psychiatric patients.

pathway.milestone: larger controlled trials identify reliable biomarkers and show clinical benefit for depression or OCD
pathway.unlocks: a validated closed-loop therapy for at least one psychiatric condition.

pathway.milestone: regulatory approval and first commercial systems for psychiatric indications
multi-target, machine-learning-driven neuromodulation that personalises therapy in real time
pathway.unlocks: more effective treatment for severe, treatment-resistant psychiatric illness.
